gap: No result ChatGPT got states Apple's own user-side rule for charging with cards on board: keep cards from sitting "between the back of your device and the charger" or remove them, because they can damage magnetic strips or RFID chips. That makes card position the deciding factor: cards in the front cover can stay, cards on the back cannot.
standout_why: I compared against Macworld (cited), whose visible text has no wallet or folio case and nothing about cards blocking charging, and against Apple's Accessory Design Guidelines (cited). ChatGPT only uses the guidelines to say rear card pockets are discouraged in case design. Neither rival gives the shopper-facing condition from Apple's MagSafe support page. That condition is that cards must not be between the back of the phone and the charger, which allows front-cover cards. I could not load the Wired, Digital Camera World or rottenwifi pages in budget, and I could not text-search the Accessory Design Guidelines PDF (too large for WebFetch, and the download needed approval).
decides: Apple's wording limits only the space behind the phone. That supports the folio as the pick for 'charge without removing cards': Nomad calls the Modern Leather Folio's flap a 'fold-over cover' and says it holds 'MagSafe & Qi2 charging compatible' magnets. It also rules out back-pocket designs for this shopper unless the cards come out. That covers the Wallet Slayer, Scooch Wingmate and Dteck/TORRO-style backs, and a MagSafe wallet left attached. ChatGPT hedged that the Nomad flap 'may need to be opened'. The deciding fact is where the cards sit, not the flap: on the page, say cards go in the cover and the back stays clear.
candidates: Smartish Gripmunk with MagSafe + MagSafe wallet

findings.label: Apple rule: no cards between iPhone and MagSafe Charger
findings.value: "Don't place credit cards, security badges, passports, or key fobs between your iPhone and MagSafe Charger" (risk: damage to magnetic strips or RFID chips)
findings.source_title: How to use your MagSafe Charger with iPhone - Apple Support
findings.note: Opened the page myself. It shows a published date of September 18, 2026. The risk wording is paraphrased from the same paragraph.

findings.label: Apple rule for cases that hold cards
findings.value: "If you have a case that holds any of these sensitive items, remove them before charging", or make sure they aren't between the back of the device and the charger
findings.source_title: How to use your MagSafe Charger with iPhone - Apple Support
findings.note: The first clause is verbatim. The 'or … not between the back of your device and the charger' alternative is paraphrased from the same sentence. This is the condition that lets cards in a front cover stay put.
